text: NestArc Go is a fictional modular insert for an adult-carried diaper bag. The launch version uses a recycled-PET outer shell, a thermoplastic-polyurethane wipe-clean lining, and removable polypropylene dividers. It measures 31 by 22 by 12 centimeters and weighs 420 grams empty. It is not a sleep product, child restraint, toy, feeding surface, or medical device.

The target direct-to-consumer MSRP is $68 for the launch version. The pilot pitch used the phrase machine washable, but the launch care instruction remains spot-clean only while repeated-wash effects on the removable base stiffener are evaluated.

The launch target is Q2 2027 in slate and moss. Committed launch scope is the base insert, six removable dividers, and two labeled wet-item pouches. An insulated bottle pod is research, not a launch commitment, and no companion mobile app is planned.

Three launch-version zipper samples completed 20,000 open-close cycles without functional failure. Three loaded seam tests failed at 17.6, 18.1, and 18.3 kilograms, averaging 18.0 kilograms. These fictional engineering checks are not a regulatory certification.
The current launch-version care instruction is spot-clean only. Machine washing was not evaluated because wash durability of the removable base stiffener's adhesive lamination remains unverified.

In a constructed exercise with 50 fictional U.S. caregivers, 36 preferred modular dividers over a single-cavity control and 31 ranked fast retrieval of wipes and spare clothes among their top three organizer needs. The small directional sample was not representative, and nobody used a production unit.

At a shown price of $68, 21 of 50 fictional participants selected too expensive, 19 selected reasonable, and 10 selected good value. This supports treating price resistance as an objection but does not prove purchase intent or demand at scale.
The fictional founder memo describes a $2.4 billion U.S. opportunity by counting all diaper bags, organizers, and travel accessories.
The fictional research note estimates $1.1 billion when limited to diaper-bag organizers and inserts; the figures use different category definitions and are not one agreed market size.

The working launch assumption is direct-to-consumer distribution at a $68 MSRP. Retail distribution, wholesale pricing, unit cost, gross margin, and international availability are not approved in this corpus.
